information.content: Xanthine oxidase inhibitor used in selected birds and reptiles for hyperuricaemia or gout support, alongside correction of hydration, diet and underlying renal or husbandry issues.
Treat the patient, not just the uric acid. Hydration, renal assessment, diet and husbandry are often the real battleground.
Aluminium hydroxide preparations are used as antacids and phosphate binders, especially where renal disease causes hyperphosphataemia.
Separate from oral fluoroquinolones, tetracyclines and digoxin. Constipation and reduced appetite can occur.
Quaternary ammonium disinfectant/antiseptic used at appropriate dilutions for flushing, nebulisation support and selected aquatic external treatments.
Low therapeutic index in fish; toxicity increases in warm or soft water. Irritant to skin and eyes.
Fish immersion anaesthetic/euthanasia agent. Effect depends on concentration, exposure time, temperature, species and water chemistry.
Use water from the animal's system, buffer pH, aerate well and test lower concentrations before treating groups.
GI cytoprotective/adsorbent used empirically for gastric irritation, ulceration or diarrhoea in selected mammals.
Do not use if obstruction, reduced gag/cough reflex, fitting or need for a specific oral antidote is present.
Glucocorticoid with high first-pass metabolism in people; used in ferrets for inflammatory bowel disease but systemic steroid effects can still occur.
Avoid intestinal perforation and severe hepatic impairment. Monitor for iatrogenic steroid effects despite first-pass metabolism.
Long-acting local anaesthetic used for regional, perineural, epidural or intrapleural analgesia. It is slower than lidocaine but longer acting.
Never give intravenously. In birds, delayed high plasma levels are a concern, so dose conservatively.
Antimuscarinic antispasmodic used in rabbits for GI or urinary tract pain only while actively investigating and treating the underlying cause.
Contraindicated in intestinal obstruction and not a treatment for rabbit ileus. It must not delay diagnosis.
Nitroimidazole antiprotozoal used mainly in pigeons for trichomoniasis/canker.
Use with hygiene, contact management and reassessment if signs persist.
NSAID used for pain and inflammation in selected mammals, birds, reptiles and fish, with species-specific evidence and caution.
Avoid dehydration, hypotension, renal disease, GI bleeding risk and concurrent steroid/NSAID therapy.
Non-selective beta blocker with alpha-1 blocking effects used only as specialist adjunct cardiac therapy.
Do not start until heart failure is stabilised. Avoid bradyarrhythmias, bronchial disease and decompensated CHF.
Selective COX-2 inhibitor used experimentally/clinically in rats and birds for inflammation/pain support.
NSAID precautions still apply: hydration, renal perfusion and GI tolerance matter.
GI adsorbent used for selected acute poisonings and toxin exposures when aspiration risk and contraindications have been considered.
Do not give before emetics or when aspiration risk is high. It binds many oral medicines as well as toxins.
Aquatic disinfectant/antimicrobial used for selected external fish disease protocols under water-quality specific guidance.
Aquatic treatments depend on species, water chemistry and system design. Specialist/aquatic guidance is needed.
Antiprotozoal/antimalarial used in selected raptors, tortoises and fish protozoal disease protocols.
Toxic to algae and many invertebrates. Do not use in reef tanks.
H1 antihistamine used for allergic disease, transfusion premedication and early anaphylaxis support in selected mammals.
May sedate and may reduce seizure threshold. Use caution with urinary retention, glaucoma or pyloroduodenal obstruction.
hCG is a reproductive hormone used for ovulation induction, persistent oestrus, ovarian cysts and avian reproductive management.
Reconstituted vials lack preservative and should be discarded within 24 hours. Anaphylactoid reactions are possible.
Calcineurin inhibitor immunosuppressant used for selected immune-mediated or inflammatory disease in exotic mammals and birds.
Major interaction nest: azoles, doxycycline, diltiazem, NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones and macrocyclic lactones need care.
Tricyclic antidepressant used with behaviour modification for anxiety-related or compulsive behaviours, including feather damaging behaviour in birds.
Avoid in tricyclic sensitivity; use caution with arrhythmias, epilepsy, glaucoma, constipation and urinary retention.
Topical imidazole antifungal used for superficial fungal disease and avian naso-sinal fungal lesions where specialist techniques are used.
Some topical products contain corticosteroids. Avoid steroid-containing products unless specifically indicated.
Anti-fibrotic/anti-inflammatory drug used in selected avian hepatic/fibrotic conditions but with a narrow safety margin.
Adverse reactions are commoner than with many drugs in this batch. Overdose can be fatal.
Ion-exchange resin used in rabbits and susceptible rodents to bind clostridial toxins after GI dysbiosis.
Can reduce absorption of digoxin, anticoagulants, diuretics, thyroxine and other oral drugs.
Aquatic copper treatment used for selected fish ectoparasites and fungal/bacterial disease, requiring free-copper monitoring.
Low therapeutic index and toxic to invertebrates, elasmobranchs, algae and many plants. Test free copper.
Alkylating cytotoxic chemotherapy used in specialist oncology protocols for selected exotic birds and reptiles.
Cytotoxic. Handle and monitor as chemotherapy; myelosuppression nadir and haemorrhagic cystitis are key hazards.
